---

### Genealogically Relevant Information

| Element | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|

| **Witness 2** | Aaltje Jans | Patronymic: *Aaltje, daughter of Jan* |

---

- **soon / zoon** — 17th-century Dutch orthography; *soon* and *zoon* are the same word. Means *son*, confirming Pieter's sex. Note this; sex isn't always stated explicitly.

- **Hendricksz** — abbreviation of *Hendrickszoon* (son of Hendrick). This is a **patronymic**, not a hereditary surname. Jan's father was named Hendrick. ---

### Original (as written)

> In nomine Dei, amen. Ego Bartholomaeus Flandrensis, senex et infirmus corpore, sanus tamen mente, lego et relinquo Joanni nepoti meo domum meam cum omnibus bonis mobilibus et immobilibus. > In the name of God, amen. I, Bartholomaeus Flandrensis, old and infirm in body, yet sound in mind, bequeath and leave to Joannes my nephew [or grandson — see note below] my house together with all goods, movable and immovable. Likewise I bequeath to Catharina, daughter of my late brother Petrus, twenty florins. Executed on the feast of Saint Gall, in the year of the Lord 1642.

---

### Term & Formula Notes

| Latin | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| *lego et relinquo* | "I bequeath and leave" | Standard testamentary doublet — a legal formula, not redundant; both verbs carry force in law |
| *nepos* | **Nephew OR grandson** | ⚠️ Critical ambiguity — see below |
| *bonis mobilibus et immobilibus* | Movable and immovable goods | Standard legal phrase; *immobilia* = real property (land, buildings); *mobilia* = personal property |
| *Item* | "Likewise" / "Also" | Standard will connector between bequests |
| *quondam* | "Late" / "formerly" | Indicates **Petrus is deceased** at the time the will was written |
| *florenos* | Florins | Gold coins; a bequest of 20 florins was a modest but meaningful legacy |
| *Actum in festo Sancti Galli* | "Executed on the feast of Saint Gall" | The feast of Saint Gall falls on **16 October** — so the document date is **16 October 1642 (1642-10-16)** |
| MDCXLII | 1642 | M(1000) + D(500) + C(100) + XL(40) + II(2) |

The Latin word *nepos* had **two distinct meanings** in period usage, and the correct reading significantly changes the family structure:

- **Classical Latin:** *nepos* = **grandson**

- Search for a sibling of Bartholomaeus with a son named Joannes (which would favor *nephew*)

### Kirchenbuch — German Parish Registers

A **Kirchenbuch** (German: *"church book"*; plural **Kirchenbücher**) is a **parish register** maintained by a Christian parish — primarily Roman Catholic and Lutheran — recording three core vital events:

- **Marriages**
- **Burials**

- Became widespread in the German-speaking world after the **Council of Trent (1563)** for Catholic parishes, and following the **Reformation** for Protestant parishes.

|---|---|
| Protestant records | Regional church archives (*Landeskirchliches Archiv*); **Archion** (subscription) |

## Translation — Brazilian Portuguese Colonial Marriage Record

---

### Original Text (as provided)

> "Aos vinte dias do mês de junho de mil setecentos e oitenta, na igreja matriz de Nossa Senhora do Rosário, recebi em matrimônio a Manuel Ferreira, natural de Lisboa, com Joana Maria, parda forra, filha natural de Inês, escrava de Antônio Gomes. Testemunhas: João da Costa e Sebastião Dias."

---

### Translation *(derivative — the original governs)*

"On the twentieth day of the month of June of one thousand seven hundred and eighty (1780-06-20), in the mother church of Our Lady of the Rosary, I received in matrimony Manuel Ferreira, native of Lisbon, with Joana Maria, freed mixed-race woman, natural daughter of Inês, slave of Antônio Gomes. Witnesses: João da Costa and Sebastião Dias."

---

### Key Terms Explained

| Original term | Literal meaning | Genealogical significance |
|---|---|---|
| *igreja matriz* | mother church / parish church | The principal parish church of the district — the record-keeping institution |
| *recebi em matrimônio* | "I received in matrimony" | Written in first person — the officiating priest is the narrator; not a civil record |
| *natural de Lisboa* | native of Lisbon | Groom's birthplace: Lisbon, Portugal — he is an immigrant to Brazil |
| *parda* | of mixed ancestry | In colonial Brazil: a person of mixed African and European descent; a formal racial-status category used in church and civil records |
| *forra* | freed / manumitted | Joana Maria had been enslaved but obtained her freedom — she is *not* described as born free (*livre*). Her free status required explicit statement in this record |
| *parda forra* combined | freed mixed-race woman | A critical legal and social status marker in colonial Brazil; distinguishes her from *parda livre* (born free) or *parda escrava* (still enslaved) |
| *filha natural* | natural daughter | **Illegitimate birth** — born outside of a recognized marriage; standard terminology in colonial Portuguese records |
| *escrava de Antônio Gomes* | slave of Antônio Gomes | Inês (Joana's mother) was still enslaved at the time of this marriage; Antônio Gomes is her enslaver, named here to identify Inês — **not** Joana's father |

---

### Genealogically Relevant Information

- **Event:** Marriage, 20 June 1780 (1780-06-20)
- **Place:** *Igreja Matriz de Nossa Senhora do Rosário* — the specific town is not stated in the record text itself
- **Groom:** Manuel Ferreira — *natural de Lisboa* (born in Lisbon, Portugal); an immigrant
- **Bride:** Joana Maria — *parda forra*; status as a freed person was formally recorded
- **Bride's mother:** Inês — enslaved (*escrava*), property of Antônio Gomes at the time of this record
- **Bride's father:** Not named — consistent with colonial practice for children of enslaved women; *filha natural* with mother only identified
- **Witnesses:** João da Costa; Sebastião Dias

---

**On "parda forra":** This precise phrasing is one of the most important status markers in Afro-Brazilian genealogy. *Forra* means she had been manumitted — freedom was granted, not inherited. |---|---|
| *infrascrito cura* | "Undersigned priest/curate" — the officiating parish priest. His name would typically appear in a record header or signature; this entry as given omits it. |
